meta.purpose: Sport-specific horizontal force-velocity norms + elite ceiling + validity gates.
meta.band_reading: p10=lower .. p50=median .. p90=upper WITHIN elite/national-team athletes; a general athlete near p40-60 here is already strong.
meta.method_note: Haugen values are Samozino split-time field-method. Do NOT compare directly to Rabita force-plate ceiling (different construct); keep them separate.

f0_nkg.note: Haugen elite ~7-10; Rabita force-plate ~9.8. Outside -> reject fit.

v0_ms.note: Haugen 7.3-10.9; Bolt ~12.3 is the human ceiling.

rfmax_pct.note: Haugen RFmax 41-52%. A naive regression giving 70-90% is broken.

elite_ceiling_rabita_2015.source: Rabita et al. 2015 Scand J Med Sci Sports; force plate; n=9 world-class (100m 9.95-10.60s)
elite_ceiling_rabita_2015.method: true ground-reaction-force, block start — a ceiling benchmark, NOT comparable to field-method norms

accel_step_reference_ettema_2016.source: Ettema et al. 2016 PLoS ONE e0159701; n=24 trained sprinters; 3D kinematics; blocks start
accel_step_reference_ettema_2016.note: Unloaded ground-truth step mechanics vs step number. Your cable-derived step length/contact should track this shape.

stride_under_load_chang_2024.source: Chang et al. 2024 PLoS ONE e0298517; n=14; motorised resistance device; 193 steps
stride_under_load_chang_2024.note: Under cable resistance: contact time lengthens, step length shortens, flight time ~unchanged.
